question: If AI devices listen and act for us in the background, how do we keep control of our own lives?
reflection: Technology that fades into the background can free our attention for people, if we stay clear about what we let it hear.

sources.subject: Meta's 816B Model Runs Locally on Two Mac Studios
Amazon wants AI to make apps obsolete

one_line: Very large open models now run on a desk instead of a data centre, while big tech pushes AI that works quietly in the background instead of inside apps.

top_stories.title: Meta's giant open model runs on two desktop computers
top_stories.what: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model that only activates about 42 billion parameters per request and reportedly runs on two high-end Mac Studios.
top_stories.why: Strong models that run fully on local hardware make it easier to analyse sensitive survey or interview data without sending it to a foreign cloud.

top_stories.title: Amazon bets on ambient AI over apps
top_stories.what: Amazon's devices chief says future computing will lean on sensor-rich devices that understand needs in the background, and its new Bee wearables record, summarise and turn conversations into reminders.
top_stories.why: Always-listening devices raise fresh questions about consent, privacy norms and trust that behavioural researchers are well placed to study.

top_stories.title: Chatbot companions and simulated empathy
top_stories.what: A widely discussed interview with sociologist Sherry Turkle explores how many adults now talk to chatbots, some as romantic partners, and the risk of accepting care from a system with no stake in us.
top_stories.why: Emotional reliance on AI is a growing behavioural question for health, youth and family policy, and a natural research topic.

saudi_lens.text: Locally runnable open models give Saudi agencies a route to capable AI that keeps sensitive data inside the Kingdom, in line with data-residency rules.
With a young, highly connected population, Saudi Arabia is a relevant place to study how teenagers and families use AI companions.

idea.title: AI companion use survey
idea.pitch: A short national survey on how young adults use chatbots for advice, comfort or company, and how that relates to wellbeing and social ties.
idea.fit: Health, youth and family services, culture sector
idea.first_step: Draft ten neutral questions on chatbot use frequency, purpose and feelings of support.

terms.definition: An AI model whose trained numbers are published so anyone can download, run and adapt it.
A model design where only a small set of specialist parts switch on for each request, so a huge model runs at the cost of a smaller one.
AI built into devices around you that senses context and acts in the background, without you opening an app.

concepts.summary: Large open models now run on local hardware, giving organisations control over their data.
Wearables and home devices that listen and act in the background instead of through apps.
People forming emotional bonds with chatbots, with open questions about wellbeing.
